claims.text: An ML interatomic potential trained on a carefully selected subset of explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics data can reproduce both solid- and liquid-phase free energies.
The ML-augmented method can retain vibrational, anharmonic, configurational, and electron–vibration free-energy contributions.
The proposed method can operate at a fraction of the computational cost of full ab initio MD or TOR-TILD.
Active learning can identify and add critical configurations near the fusion transition to the MLIP training set.
An MLIP trained in this way can reliably generate free-energy surfaces for both solid and fluid states.
CoCrFeNiTa_x with x from 0.0 to 1.0 is a high-entropy-alloy system suitable for the proposed extension.
The method is expected to apply from elemental and binary metals through moderately complex multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Training snapshots should bracket the melting temperature and represent both relevant phases.
Vibrational and configurational entropy make material contributions to the thermodynamic stabilization of CoCrFeNiTa_x.
The learned potential preserves the important short- and long-range interactions and entropy terms of the underlying ab initio description.
Interpolation by the MLIP between ab initio training points retains relevant electronic effects.
Active learning keeps the phase-transition region sufficiently sampled.
Using the MLIP reduces the number of costly ab initio MD simulations required.
The resulting free energies and derived thermodynamic observables will have fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio MD.
The method will be at least approximately ten times faster than explicit ab initio MD.
The method will provide higher throughput than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The proposed reliability range extends from below melting to approximately 1.1–1.2 times the melting temperature.

Transferability to highly disordered liquids, strong anharmonicity, strong electron–vibration coupling, or extreme multicomponent chemistry is uncertain and depends on training-set representativeness.
A decisive benchmark compares MLIP and full ab initio MD solid–liquid free-energy differences, melting temperatures, heat capacities, and entropy contributions for Cu–Ni and CoCrFeNiTa_x.

The hypothesis is falsified if phase free-energy differences or transition temperatures differ from ab initio MD by more than 10%, or if derived thermodynamic observables are inconsistent with the reference.
